_readme: Hand-written cases for the sentence a page shows about when a route was traced.
Read by tests/test_render_map.py and tests/js/map.test.js, so Python and JavaScript
are held to the same answers and cannot drift apart. Every 'note' below is a literal
somebody worked out on paper; no test computes its own expectation.
A case added here fails both test suites until both sides handle it.
The rule: silence when the trace was taken within the run's own length plus fifteen
minutes of the run starting, because a trace runs after the probes stop and takes a
minute or two. Otherwise the date and the gap, floored to the largest whole unit.
The gap is measured from the end of the run, which is where the window ends too.

The last two cases carry no offset. Python reads such a stamp as UTC; `new Date` would read it as the reader's own local time. One sits just after midnight UTC and one just before, so any zone at all shifts one of them across a date boundary and fails. tests/test_explorer_js.py runs the node suite under UTC+14 and UTC-11 to make that bite.

cases.why: no stamp at all: a trace made before the field existed
cases.note: When this route was traced was not recorded.

cases.why: the ordinary case: traced 65 s after a 60 s run started, so 5 s after it ended
exactly on the window: 60 s of run plus 900 s of grace is 960 s, and this is 960 s
one second past the window: 961 s from the start, so 901 s after the run ended, floored to 15 minutes
cases.note: Traced on 2026-08-30, 15 minutes after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.

cases.why: hours: the run ended at 14:01 and the trace ran at 18:01, four hours later
cases.note: Traced on 2026-08-30, 4 hours after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.

cases.why: one hour, singular: the run ended at 14:01 and the trace ran at 15:06, so 1 h 5 min
cases.note: Traced on 2026-08-30, 1 hour after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.

cases.why: one day, singular: the run ended at 14:01 on the 30th, the trace ran at 15:00 the next day
cases.note: Traced on 2026-08-31, 1 day after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.

cases.why: the run this whole change came from: leeds_bt 13:59 on 2026-08-30, re-traced on publish eleven days later
cases.note: Traced on 2026-09-10, 11 days after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.

cases.why: eleven and a half days is still eleven days: the gap is floored, never rounded up
cases.note: Traced on 2026-09-11, 11 days after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.

cases.why: no duration recorded: the window falls back to the grace alone, and 10 min is inside it
no duration recorded and 20 min later, so outside the 15 min window
cases.note: Traced on 2026-08-30, 20 minutes after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.

cases.why: a --longer run: 600 s of run plus grace is 1500 s, and this trace is 1400 s in
offsets are normalised before subtracting: 15:00+01:00 is 14:00Z, so this trace is 30 s in
the date shown is the UTC date: 00:30 on the 11th in Berlin is 22:30 on the 10th in UTC
cases.note: Traced on 2026-09-10, 11 days after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.

cases.why: a Z suffix means UTC, and both languages must read it
a stamp nobody can read is a stamp we do not have, and must not throw
cases.note: When this route was traced was not recorded.

cases.why: a run with no start either: still an answer, still not a crash
cases.note: When this route was traced was not recorded.

cases.why: a trace stamped before its own run is a corrupt record: say nothing rather than nonsense
no offset means UTC, not the reader's own clock: 00:10 shifts back a day in any zone ahead of UTC
cases.note: Traced on 2026-09-10, 10 days after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.

cases.why: the same rule the other way: 23:50 shifts forward a day in any zone behind UTC
cases.note: Traced on 2026-09-10, 11 days after this run, so it may not be the path the run took.
